0.long_answer: Canavan disease is an inherited leukodystrophy that is characterized by severe deterioration of myelin. This condition is caused by a deficiency in the aspartoacylase enzyme, which normally breaks down N-acetylaspartate (NAA). When aspartoacylase is deficient, NAA accumulates in the brain, leading to an imbalance in osmolytes and subsequent damage to the myelin sheath. The disrupted metabolism of NAA not only affects the formation of myelin-associated lipids but also contributes to the degeneration of neurological function observed in Canavan disease.
